turns.text: ok this isnt a task really, i just need to think out loud for a sec. is that ok
Of course. Think out loud as much as you like. What's on your mind?
so i have a second round video interview with harrowgate distribution on nov 18. lowkey excited and also ngl i feel sick about it. i froze on a phone screen before so my brain keeps replaying that

Excited and nervous at the same time makes sense, especially when a second round means they already like what they saw on paper. The freeze you're remembering was one call. Is the nervous part more about the interview itself, or about what it would mean if it goes well or badly?

both i guess. my sister sunita got me the referral through a former colleague of hers. im really grateful but now i also dont want to let her down. like she vouched for me and if i blank on th first question thats on her too 💀

That's a lot to carry. A referral gets your foot in the door, but the second round is already about you, and she vouched for you because she believes you can handle it. Being grateful and feeling the pressure can both be true. Is there anything about the interview itself you feel okay about?

i did a research outline on them friday so thats something. anyway just got back from my parents. came home with a tub of dal from my mom like every sunday, and she asked about the interview about four times. then at langar gurpreet uncle asked again if im gonna get my cdl just in case. so apparently the whole plan is: interview, dal, truck

Ha, a solid backup plan if you ever need one. It sounds like everyone at dinner is invested in you, which is nice and also exhausting when you're already anxious. Do you want to think about how to answer when people ask, so it feels less like being quizzed?
honestly yeah. everyone has my career mapped out except me apparently. maybe just a short line like 'its on the 18th, ill update you after'

That works well. It's honest, it sets a clear point when you'll share news, and it stops the repeat questions. You could add something like 'I'm prepping, but I'd rather not talk through it until after.' The interview is still more than a week away, and you've already done real prep with your research outline.
